facts: Adolph Rupp was Kentucky's head men's basketball coach from 1930 to 1972.
His career record at Kentucky was 876-190 (.822 winning percentage) — the most wins of any men's NCAA Division I coach at the time of his retirement.
He won four NCAA championships: 1948, 1949, 1951, and 1958.
He also won the 1946 NIT championship.
He won 27 Southeastern Conference regular-season titles and 13 SEC tournament titles.
Kentucky made 20 NCAA tournament appearances and reached 6 Final Fours under Rupp.
He was named National Coach of the Year five times (1950, 1954, 1959, 1966, 1970).
His nickname was 'the Baron of the Bluegrass.'
The 1948 NCAA champions were nicknamed the 'Fabulous Five'; the 1958 NCAA champions were nicknamed the 'Fiddlin' Five.'
Kentucky did not field a team for the 1952-53 season after NCAA sanctions connected to a point-shaving scandal of that era.
Rupp's 1966 team reached the NCAA championship game and lost to Texas Western, whose all-Black starting lineup made the game a landmark moment in the integration of college basketball.
Kentucky's home arena, Rupp Arena (opened 1976), is named in his honor.
